$comment: Authoritative attestation reference for the production publicai-gateway CVM. Fetched at runtime by the /proof page. composeHash was read back from the CVM's RTMR3 event log on 2026-09-23 (nonce-bound quote, imr 3, event compose-hash) and cross-checked against the Phala control-plane API; both report 4d76028e. The sub2api image digest is the linux/amd64 child of the cosign-signed proof-v42 index (INDEX b804e3de) built by publish-tee-images run 35830624113 from commit 5839d21a4; the attestor image is deliberately left at its proof-v20 pin because deploy/attestor carries no change since that release. HOW THE IMAGE DIGEST WAS RESOLVED, stated plainly because proof-v38 got this wrong and took production down for about 15 minutes: resolved with deploy/phala/pin-amd64.sh (parses `imagetools inspect --raw` as JSON, matches on the platform field); re-checked with the same script's --verify mode after editing compose; and the pinned digest was then actually docker-pulled and inspected - amd64/linux, entrypoint /app/docker-entrypoint.sh present, 140 MB - which an attestation-manifest cannot satisfy. WHAT THIS RELEASE CHANGES: three hardcoded OpenAI model ids that all pointed at gpt-5.4, which upstream retired on 2026-08-31 for Codex when signed in with a ChatGPT account (the official API, and Codex driven by your own API key, were unaffected - so the value only broke on one of the two paths). Supply accounts authenticate over exactly the path that was retired, so the supply-admission probe could not succeed for any OpenAI contributor. supplyProbeDefaultModelOpenAI (admission probe), openai.DefaultTestModel (admin test-connection, APIKey Responses capability probe, pricing last-resort fallback) and the gateway.openai_compact_model default all move to gpt-5.6-terra, the replacement upstream designates. terra was chosen over the two other candidates because it is the only one that is reachable on both the official API and Codex, carries a price entry in model_prices_and_context_window.json (the pricing fallback looks that constant up there, and a miss degrades to no price), has no Codex CLI version floor (gpt-6-astra requires >= 0.153.0) and is not plan-gated (gpt-5.6-sol returns a deterministic 400 on ChatGPT accounts). The Claude-to-OpenAI messages-dispatch defaults still name gpt-5.4 and were deliberately NOT changed: which OpenAI model should serve an Opus-shaped request is a product decision rather than a mechanical fix, and that path is gated by groups.allow_messages_dispatch, which the schema defaults to false. WHY THE BUG SURVIVED THREE WEEKS, recorded because the mechanism matters more than the constant: on the Anthropic side a probe that finds no quota rejects the account at attach with a dedicated error code, so the first contributor to hit it surfaces it immediately; on the OpenAI side supplyProbeNoQuota returns false unconditionally, so a failed probe neither rejects nor alerts - the account simply stays in pending_review and is re-probed every 15 minutes indefinitely. Combined with the fact that production has never held a single real OpenAI supply account, nobody could step on it. The unit test that pinned the constant asserted it equalled the string literal, which merely restates the constant and cannot know upstream retired it; it is replaced here by an assertion that the probe model exists in openai.DefaultModelIDs(), which catches a typo but still cannot catch a retirement. There is NO schema migration in this release and no ent model or dependency-wiring change - the diff is three string constants, their comments, and two test updates. Claude traffic is unaffected by construction rather than by inspection: matchOpenAIModel is only reached when the model name starts with gpt-, and Claude account tests resolve claude.DefaultTestModel, which is untouched. Verified before rollout: go build, go vet, and the full tagged unit suite across all 51 backend packages, green. VERIFICATION SCOPE, stated honestly: composeHash and osImageHash were each read back from the live enclave, and composeHash was cross-checked against two independent sources; the image digest was resolved mechanically and then confirmed by pulling it. The cosign keyless signature was NOT verified locally for this release - cosign is not installed on the release machine - though the signing workflow run succeeded and anyone can verify certificate identity https://github.com/FiiLabs/sub2api/.github/workflows/publish-tee-images.yml@refs/heads/feat/two-sided-market plus the embedded githubWorkflowSha against the sourceCommit below. Two further limitations a reader should not have to infer: no postgres backup was taken before this rollout, unlike previous releases, on the grounds that the change carries no migration and cannot touch data, with rollback being a re-pin of the previous digest 00b7a80a; and the fix itself is NOT verified end to end, because that requires binding a real ChatGPT account and production has none. What is proven here is that the retired id is gone and that its replacement is a real, priced, non-gated model on both paths - not that a contributor can now complete onboarding. That check remains open. Earlier in this line: proof-v41 (contributor privacy note and worked earnings example), proof-v40 (configurable homepage campaign banner), proof-v39 (per-campaign online-day buckets, new-contributor-only rewards, idle account re-check), proof-v38 (supply incentive rules engine), proof-v37, v36, v35, v34, v33, v32, v31, v29..v15. osImageHash, appId and instanceId are unchanged; the deploy passed --no-dev-os explicitly and the control plane confirms is_dev false after the rollout. This rollout completed in 79 seconds with no incident; apex1.us, api.apex1.us and the public stats endpoint all returned 200 immediately afterwards.
